solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Strike after firm offers minimal money to Russians

indicators.note: after places the word for strike behind the word for firm

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm
to peck is to strike with the beak

explanation.surface: A company offers its Russian workers a pittance after a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A kopeck, also spelt this way, is a hundredth of a rouble, the smallest Russian coin.

clue.text: Vehicles crossing line? We may deal with them!

definitions.text: Vehicles crossing line? We may deal with them!

indicators.note: crossing means the vehicles word straddles the letter for line

parts.note: campers are motor homes, camper vans

explanation.surface: Parking enforcers boast that cars over the yellow line are theirs to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is spoken by the answer: cars parked over a line are what they deal with.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheel-clamping enforcers immobilise illegally parked cars, so badly parked vehicles are their business.

clue.text: Material put down under piano

indicators.note: under places the words for put down below the piano letter in this down clue

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
laid means put down

explanation.surface: Fabric is laid down beneath a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan twill cloth, a checked woollen fabric, is a kind of material.

clue.text: Maximum waterproofing, as one might say?

indicators.note: as one might say tells us the waterproofing word is spoken, giving a word that sounds identical

parts.note: sealing something makes it watertight

explanation.surface: Asks whether total waterproofing is what someone might call it.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper limit, such as a price cap, is the highest permitted level.

clue.text: Wise man met with expression of surprise and resistance

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise
a mage is a magus, a wise man or sorcerer

explanation.surface: A sage is greeted with a gasp of astonishment and some pushback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' looks like a third wordplay piece (R), but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical resistance measured in ohms is called by this technical term.

clue.text: Hospital notice outside big building set up to show emergency landing spot?

indicators.note: outside means the hospital and notice letters enclose the building word

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
an ad is a notice or advertisement

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the building word is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building

explanation.surface: A hospital sign around a tall building shows where air ambulances should land.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat marked area where helicopters touch down, often on hospital roofs for urgent arrivals.

clue.text: Novel gas energy supply

indicators.note: supply is read as the adverb of supple, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A new form of gas energy delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, and 'supply' a noun; both are misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Brontë's first book, about a governess, is a classic Victorian novel.

clue.text: Cardinal having great influence, not weak

indicators.note: not means the letter for weak is dropped

parts.note: weighty means important, having great influence

explanation.surface: A powerful churchman who is anything but feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a prelate; it means a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are counting numbers, and four score is one of them.

clue.text: Monkey died in tree

parts.note: a tamarin is a small South American monkey
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A monkey has perished up in a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical leguminous tree whose pods give a sour pulp used in cooking.

clue.text: Pull in man who must meet wedding guests in reception area

parts.note: to draw is to pull

parts.words: man who must meet wedding guests
parts.note: the groom greets guests at the wedding reception

explanation.surface: A man at a wedding must draw guests into the reception hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal room for receiving visitors in a large house, originally the withdrawing room.

clue.text: Story about horse gets certain amount of newspaper coverage

indicators.note: about means the word for story goes around the horse

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A tale concerning a racehorse earns a few column inches in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper space is measured by the number of printed lines, a variant of lineage.

clue.text: Party with old man rolling over? One can't stand on feet

indicators.note: rolling over turns the party and the old man round together, so they read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party
pa is father, one's old man

explanation.surface: An elderly man at a party has keeled over and cannot stay upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One can't stand on feet' sounds like a drunk partygoer, but it describes a creature with no feet at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoologists use this word for a footless animal, such as a snake or certain eels, which therefore has nothing to stand on.

clue.text: One vessel turning back, river location being unsuitable

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: turning back means the word for vessel is read backwards

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
the Po is Italy's longest river
a site is a location

explanation.surface: A boat turning round at some spot on a river is badly placed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of place or irrelevant is not apt; the word is a negative of apposite.

clue.text: Musician who is possible generator of groan

parts.note: grinding up the letters of the instrument's name, an organ, rearranges them to make groan

explanation.surface: A musician whose playing tends to make listeners groan.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: something that grinds (shuffles) ORGAN would produce GROAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A street performer who turns the handle of a barrel organ is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Outside workroom store a broken instrument no longer used

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters surround the workroom word
broken means the letters of store and a are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: a lab is a laboratory, a workroom

explanation.surface: Outside a workshop lies a broken, obsolete instrument from the store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store a' reads as a shop and an article, but the two words together are anagram fodder; 'broken' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This old navigational device measured the altitude of stars and has long been superseded.

clue.text: Discovery when having inner existence manipulated

indicators.note: having inner means the discovery word holds the existence word inside it

parts.note: a find is a discovery
esse is Latin for being, used in English to mean existence

explanation.surface: A discovery that one's inner life has been manipulated.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle something with delicate skill or cunning is to manage it adroitly, i.e. to manipulate it.

clue.text: Poor mechanical device sticky inside? Object when you can't nail it

definitions.text: Object when you can't nail it

indicators.note: inside puts the word for sticky between the words for poor and device

parts.note: thin means poor or meagre
a jig is a device that holds work and guides tools
gummy means sticky

explanation.surface: A shoddy contraption with glue inside it, a thing you can't nail together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nail it' suggests carpentry with the device, but means pinning down the name of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A jokey placeholder word used for any object whose real name you cannot recall.

clue.text: One of the gang who knows how you could cook pork, we hear?

definitions.text: One of the gang who knows

indicators.note: we hear signals that the cooking phrase is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: pork is often cooked in cider, a classic pairing

explanation.surface: A gang member who knows a good recipe for pork.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone within a group or organisation with privileged knowledge of its workings.

clue.text: Dull lad awkwardly holding one lass waltzing?

indicators.note: holding means the dull word and jumbled lad together enclose the letter for one

parts.note: mat or matt means dull, not glossy

indicators.note: awkwardly means the letters of lad are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A clumsy, dull lad holding a girl during a waltz.
explanation.definitionFit: Waltzing Matilda is the famous Australian song, so the girl's name is the one who goes waltzing.

clue.text: First Minister losing his head — a bit of a fruitcake?

indicators.note: losing his head means the politician's surname drops its first letter

parts.note: Alex Salmond was First Minister of Scotland, the head of its devolved government

explanation.surface: A political leader losing his head, suggesting he is a little crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruitcake' suggests an eccentric person, but here it is a cake containing nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts are typical fruitcake ingredients, and this is one such nut.

clue.text: Swaggering fellows left for controversial pursuit

parts.note: bloods are dashing, swaggering young men of fashion
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: Some cocky young men have departed in favour of a contentious hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting, coursing and similar activities that kill animals for entertainment are hotly debated pastimes.

clue.text: Ancient language comes from bloke without hesitation

indicators.note: without means the hesitation sound is removed from the word for bloke

parts.note: geezer is British slang for a man, a bloke
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: An old tongue spoken by a fellow who never stumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ge'ez is the classical Ethiopian tongue, still used in Ethiopian church liturgy.

clue.text: Huge number losing love somewhere along the line for Russian author

indicators.note: losing means the letter for love is taken away
somewhere along the line says the lost letter comes from within the word rather than an end

parts.note: a googol is ten to the power of a hundred
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A vast quantity losing affection at some point, for a Russian writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol wrote Dead Souls and The Government Inspector, a major Russian writer.

clue.text: Joke about conflict from one who'd always avoid it?

indicators.note: about means the joke word wraps around the conflict

parts.note: cod as a verb means to hoax or joke
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A wisecrack about war from a pacifist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' refers back to 'conflict': the definition is someone who shuns a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A person lacking courage is the sort who always dodges a fight.

clue.text: Poem by mum is full of empty words in a language few of us understand

definitions.text: a language few of us understand

indicators.note: by sets the word for mum beside the poem

parts.note: ma is mother, mum

indicators.note: is full of means the empty words sit inside the poem

parts.note: a lay is a narrative poem or song
gas is idle, empty talk

explanation.surface: Mum's poem is all hot air, written in an obscure tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the national language of Madagascar, spoken by very few outside that island.

clue.text: Pedestrian gets back in time avoiding middle of car

indicators.note: in puts the word for back inside what is left of the time word
avoiding means the central letter of car is left out of the time word

parts.note: a day is a period of time

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of car

parts.note: rear means back

explanation.surface: A pedestrian returns in time, steering clear of the middle of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' looks like a walker on the road, but it is an adjective meaning dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means dull and uninspired, i.e. tedious.

clue.text: Weak and unwell, coming back into home?

indicators.note: into puts the reversed word inside the home word

parts.note: pad is slang for one's home

indicators.note: coming back means the word for unwell is read backwards

parts.note: ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Someone feeble and sick returns home.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale, wan complexion suggests feebleness; the word also describes insipid, lacking vigour.
